title: Data Center Boom Raises Issue of Who Pays for Grid, RWE Says
source_used: Briefs Finance, relaying a Bloomberg interview with RWE's chief executive (7 Oct 2026); Bloomberg is the reporter
key_facts: RWE chief executive Markus Krebber said in a Bloomberg interview on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026 that Europe needs bigger grids, and that more demand requires more grid construction and dependable capacity.

He said those creating the extra load are not paying for it right now, and policymakers should consider directing grid expansion costs to the sources of that new demand instead of spreading them across all customers.
Data centres are ready to pay more for electricity, which could tighten competition for supply and pressure consumers and energy-heavy industries.
So far Europe has not seen the same scale of power price impact as the US.
Moody's has estimated the US AI buildout will require about $110 billion of new power plants (as cited by Briefs Finance).
RWE has pinpointed more than 10 prospective locations across Europe that it could develop and later sell.
quote_evidence: In a Bloomberg interview on Wednesday, CEO Markus Krebber put it simply: more demand requires more grid construction and dependable capacity.

He said those creating the extra load are not footing the bill right now, adding that policymakers should consider directing the grid expansion costs to the sources of that new demand instead of spreading them across all customers.
So far, Europe has not seen the same scale of power price impact as the US.
why_it_matters_hint: Who pays for grid upgrades when data centres add demand: the firms creating it or every customer's bill.
